summary: This work demonstrates an end-to-end real-time decoder for a universal fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computer capable of processing workloads with up to 408 logical qubits and one million logical $T$ gates using only a single conventional CPU. The decoder achieves computational stretch (additional syndrome-extraction cycles due to decoding latency) below 0.3% at $p_{	ext{CNOT}}=10^{-4}$ and below 12% at $p_{	ext{CNOT}}=5	imes10^{-4}$ across all tested benchmarks.
motivation: Real-time decoding at MegaQuOp scale (millions of gates, hundreds of logical qubits) remains a major challenge for fault-tolerant quantum computing because syndrome data is generated faster than classical decoders can process it, risking exponential computation slowdown from decoding backlogs.
method: The authors exploit the walking-cat architecture (WCA) to implement a dual sliding-window decoder (error decoder with 5-SEC window and outcome decoder with 2-SEC window) that reuses a static Tanner graph with dynamically updated priors for on-the-fly detector-error-model generation, avoiding expensive graph reconstruction. Beam search decoders are optimized via reformulated belief-propagation state storage (posterior log-likelihood ratios per error node instead of per Tanner-graph edge) to enable concurrent execution of 12 decoder instances on a single 2024 Apple M4 Max CPU.
result: For MIPT (1.09 million $T$ gates, 102 logical qubits, 1 ms/SEC budget) and Heisenberg n266 (555k $T$ gates, 408 logical qubits, 5 ms/SEC budget), stretch is 0.24% and 0.02% respectively at $p_{	ext{CNOT}}=10^{-4}$, rising to 11.5% and 0.7% at $p_{	ext{CNOT}}=5	imes10^{-4}$, with mean stretch-episode lengths of 2.8–10.9 SECs and 99.9th percentile lengths of 31–252 SECs.
